name: AI trade jitters
backstory: The biggest AI-linked tech firms hold up so much of the [[S&P 500]] that doubts about AI hit the whole market. Nvidia's CEO left on Nov 12, a selloff followed, official papers warned that AI [[valuation]]s look stretched, and the index fell four straight weeks. Then Nvidia's board approved Huang's return, the Nasdaq jumped 6.51% on Monday, and the S&P 500 had its best day in more than a year.
today: Tuesday gave back a good part of that bounce, with Nvidia and Anthropic ending sharply lower. Anthropic fell 6.5% to $81.91, below its $83 IPO price, and it has been sliding since it opened at $111.50 on Nov 19. Dell reported sales that more than doubled on AI server demand and announced a $25 billion buyback, yet the group still fell, which suggests good news was already expected. Meanwhile Huang's return leaves open regulatory questions and an investigation, Republicans worry about his reported ties to a suspected Chinese spy, and BNP Paribas warned that a glut of memory chips could hurt Micron.

name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and pushed up [[headline inflation]], so central banks must decide whether the price jump fades or leaks into wages and services. Euro area inflation hit 4%, the Bank of England hiked to 4%, and the Fed sits at 3.875%.
today: Headlines argued that Wall Street's 2027 earnings hopes depend on the Fed easing in December, while inflation makes that unlikely, a bit like 2018 without a Fed rescue. CIBC said the Bank of Canada could [[rate hike]] again in December because Governor Macklem keeps stressing inflation risks. In France, the central bank governor still expects growth even though recession risk is in the news, pointing to defense, aerospace and electricity. Recent Fed talk (Williams on higher rates 'over time', Waller on the Dec 8 and 9 meeting, Cook on oil staying high) still frames the debate.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout, and markets asked how divided government might change tariffs, spending and the dollar. The dollar then had its biggest rally since 2024, with headlines crediting hawkish Fed bets and not the election.
today: The dollar index slipped 0.47% to 103.83 after hitting a 20-month high, strongest since March 2025, and Reuters said it gave back much of Monday's gains as the Nvidia-fueled AI rally faded. The Canadian dollar bounced from a 19-month low as the greenback retreated. J.P. Morgan said the dollar could rise further in 2027 if the Fed lifts rates, and consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 after the Democratic wins, although inflation worries persist.

name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The conflict began in early 2026 and cut global oil output by 12 mb/d in March, but prices stayed below records because stored oil filled the gap. The IEA says the Hormuz shock lifted the world's oil and gas import bill 25% to $1.6 trillion.
today: WTI crude rose 1.67% to 81.51 after Monday's drop to a low not seen since August, and energy stocks advanced late in the day. The headlines don't explain the bounce clearly, so it may simply be a pause after a sharp fall. Pump prices dropped to their lowest level since March, which is welcome news before Thanksgiving, and Trump has suggested the recent decline in gas prices has political motives, with one headline using the phrase 'a giant hoax'.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the currency market, including a record $50 billion in one day. The BOJ's 1.25% rate is 2.625 percentage points below the Fed's 3.875%, which encourages selling yen to hold dollars. Japan's economy unexpectedly shrank in Q3 as energy costs bit.
today: USD/JPY was 159.32, down 0.04%, so the yen was little changed. The BOJ chief played down soft consumption data and signaled a near-term rate hike. Japan's inflation accelerated, and the country posted a sixth straight monthly trade deficit. A Reuters-style analysis says BOJ ambiguity on the path of hikes could tempt yen bears. In Friday's Asian session, the Nikkei fell 2.9% on chip and metals stocks.
